subject: Hospitality
title: The Lobby as Living Room
description: A fast breakdown of The Lobby as Living Room for builders.

hook.text: Hotel lobbies used to be pass-through spaces. Now they're designed as social hubs—the hotel's living room for guests and locals.

buildup.text: W Hotels pioneered the 'Living Room' concept: lobbies with bars, music, comfortable seating.

discovery.text: The Lobby as Living Room reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: The lobby-as-living-room blurs the line between hotel and café. Non-guests now use hotel lobbies as co-working spaces.

climax.text: This shift forced a redesign of the front desk. Some hotels eliminated it entirely, replacing it with roaming staff with tablets.

punchline.text: No front desk, just sofas and a bar. The lobby became the product.

quiz.question: How much more do guests who spend time in the lobby tend to spend?
options: 40% more on food, drink, and services
